To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complexity of kinematics of a legged animal increases through ground contact and that a low complexity of feed-forward control in combination with compliant legged hardware is sufficient for level ground locomotion.

a modular, feed forward locomotion controller with low complexity kinematic patterns is sufficient to generate self-stable and even self-stabilizing quadruped locomotion, and that the complexity of the kinematic patterns increases with the complexity of the mechanical system.
the kinematic patterns of quadruped locomotion can be described by a low number of primitives, which are different for in-air stepping and on ground locomotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what is the complexity of kinematics in quadrupedal walking?
the role of body and leg dynamics in the complexity and variability of kinematic gait patterns.
a modular, feedforward locomotion controller for a small, compliant quadruped robot, and its role in the complexity of leg kinematics in in-air stepping and onground locomotion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the complexity of the locomotor control system of a quadrupedic robot is determined by the complexity of the task (i.e. locomotion on different terrain) and the complexity of the mechanical system (i.e. the legged robot).

the role of body and leg dynamics in legged locomotion is to reduce the complexity of the kinematic patterns, while the role of the control system is to increase the complexity of the control patterns.
the complexity of kinematics of a legged robot depends on the interaction of the legged hardware, and the complexity of motor control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a very low-complexity, feed-forward control is sufficient for stable and self-stabilization quadruped locomotion, when combined with compliant, legged hardware.
a very low-complexity feed-forward locomotion control can result in kinematic patterns with a high complexity, which is a result of the interaction of the compliant legged hardware and the ground.

the role of the body dynamics in the emergence of complex kinematics in a quadrupod robot with compliant legs is significant, and that the body dynamics is a crucial factor in the emergence of the complexity of kinematics in quadruped locomotion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of kinematics of legged locomotion is determined by a combination of motor and mechanical factors, and not solely by motor factors as previously suggested in literature.

body dynamics play an important role in the kinematics and complexity of kinematic leg patterns during locomotion, which has to be considered in the design of locomotion controllers for compliant legged robots.
a very low-complexity, feed-forward locomotor controller is sufficient to produce kinematically rich, dynamically stable locomotion of a quadrupod with compliant legs.
